experiments.description: Adding a learnable write gate with sigmoid activation will allow the model to dynamically control memory update magnitude, improving retention of associative patterns.

hypothesis.hypothesis: Adding a learnable write gate with sigmoid activation will allow the model to dynamically control memory update magnitude, improving retention of associative patterns.
hypothesis.rationale: Hyperparameters have been exhausted: learning_rate sweeps (iter_2,4,7,8,9,11) and batch_size sweeps (iter_6,10) failed to improve beyond EM=0.0234. n_mem_tokens sweep (iter_5) established baseline. The current fixed write_gate (0.5) lacks adaptability; a sigmoid-gated mechanism will enable layer-specific memory update control.
hypothesis.instruction: In MemoryAugmentedLayer.__init__, replace self.write_gate = nn.Parameter(torch.tensor(0.5)) with: self.write_gate = nn.Linear(hidden_size, 1) and add self.gate_activation = nn.Sigmoid(). In MemoryAugmentedLayer.forward, change 'memory = memory + self.write_gate * write_residual' to: 'gate_input = torch.mean(hidden_states_normed, dim=1); gate_value = self.gate_activation(self.write_gate(gate_input)); memory = memory + gate_value * write_residual'. This makes the write gate adaptive based on input content.

experiments.description: Adding a learnable memory initialization instead of random Gaussian will provide better starting point for storing associative patterns.

hypothesis.hypothesis: Adding a learnable memory initialization instead of random Gaussian will provide better starting point for storing associative patterns.
hypothesis.rationale: Hyperparameters have been extensively explored: learning_rate sweeps [0.0001, 0.001, 0.01, 0.1] in iterations 9, 11, 14, 16, 17; n_mem_tokens sweep [16, 32, 64, 128] in iteration 18; n_layer increased from 4 to 6 in iteration 13; max_steps increased to 50000 in iteration 15. All sweeps returned EM=-1.0 indicating training instability rather than poor hyperparameter choice. Random memory initialization may prevent the model from effectively storing associative patterns from the start.
hypothesis.instruction: In MemoryAugmentedLayer.__init__, replace the random initialization of initial_memory_state with a learnable parameter. Change from: self.register_buffer('initial_memory_state', initial_memory) to self.initial_memory_state = nn.Parameter(torch.randn(1, num_mem_tokens, hidden_size) / math.sqrt(hidden_size)). Also modify RMCACell to pass the config's num_mem_tokens instead of creating initial_memory there.
